name: Plymouth-Canton Community Schools
calendarType: Wayne County common-calendar district with a three-day kindergarten opening, grade-band half days, P-CEP finals and testing schedules, and a separate Starkweather Academy calendar
seoDescription: Reviewed P-CCS dates, three-day kindergarten opening, K-5 half days, P-CEP finals and testing, Starkweather exceptions, bell times, breaks, and PDFs.
districtFact: P-CCS is not a one-clock district. Its family calendar distinguishes elementary, middle-school, P-CEP half-day, P-CEP exam-day, and Starkweather dismissal times, while the three Canton, Plymouth, and Salem high schools share Michigan's only educational park and Starkweather Academy publishes a separate quarterly calendar.

about.title: Three High Schools Share One 305-Acre Educational Park
about.content: Plymouth-Canton Educational Park, or P-CEP, is the only educational park in Michigan. Canton, Plymouth, and Salem high schools share the 305-acre campus and its course offerings, while about 6,200 students use the Park each school day.

about.title: A Home High School Does Not Limit P-CEP Classes
about.content: P-CCS randomly assigns each student a Canton, Plymouth, or Salem home school for counseling, records, sports, and graduation. Students can take courses across all three buildings, so the district calendar's P-CEP finals and testing labels apply across the shared campus rather than to one neighborhood high school.

about.title: Kindergarten Opens in Three Short Steps
about.content: The first student day is a half day for all K-12 students. Kindergarten then remains on half days for the next two school days while grades 1-12 move to full days, creating a three-half-day opening sequence for kindergarten families.

about.title: Half Day Has Five Published Clocks
about.content: The family calendar lists separate half-day dismissal times for elementary schools, middle schools, regular P-CEP half days, P-CEP exam days, and Starkweather Academy. A grade-band label is therefore necessary before a family can determine pickup time.

about.title: Starkweather Uses Its Own Quarter Rhythm
about.content: Starkweather Academy serves alternative and adult learners and operates four quarters with registration, incentive, conference, contract, and records days that can differ from the K-12 family calendar. The district PDF supplies Starkweather bell times, but its academy calendar remains the attendance authority for enrolled students.

about.title: Wayne County Sets the Shared Break Framework
about.content: P-CCS participates in the Wayne County five-year common calendar developed with 33 county school districts. The common calendar establishes selected professional-development and winter, mid-winter, and spring-break dates; P-CCS then adds its own opening sequence, conferences, testing, finals, and other local dates.

calendarNotes: P-CCS begins with a half day for all K-12 students and two more kindergarten-only half days. K-5 conference and planning half days do not shorten middle-school or P-CEP attendance unless the event explicitly names those grades. P-CEP uses a 10:35 a.m. regular half-day dismissal and a separate 10:40 a.m. exam-day dismissal. The three comprehensive high schools share one educational park, so P-CEP testing and finals instructions span Canton, Plymouth, and Salem. Starkweather appears in the district bell-time table but publishes its own quarterly attendance calendar. Wayne County's common calendar explains the shared break framework but does not replace P-CCS's local family calendar. The live district Google calendar and individual school calendars carry events and changes beyond the one-page PDF.

planningTips.title: Planning with the P-CCS Family Calendar
content: Plan for three kindergarten half days at the start of the year: the all-student opening half day plus two kindergarten-only half days.
Match each shortened day to its printed scope: K-5, grades 6-8, grades 9-12, or all K-12 students.
Use the P-CEP exam-day time for finals dates; it ends five minutes later than the regular P-CEP half-day schedule.
Treat afternoon parent-teacher conferences as the reason for a K-5 half day, not as an additional full-day district closure.
Keep P-CEP state-testing dates separate from half days unless the family calendar explicitly says students are dismissed early.
Starkweather families should use the academy's quarterly calendar for registration, incentive, contract, records, and graduation dates.
Subscribe to the official P-CCS Google calendar for live updates, but keep the student's school calendar for activities, athletics, and building-specific events.

livingHere.intro: P-CCS serves a Wayne County community whose school map ranges from 14 neighborhood elementary schools to a shared three-high-school educational park and an alternative academy.

highlights.label: 14 elementary schools
highlights.detail: The official district overview lists 14 elementary campuses with geographic attendance areas.

highlights.label: 5 middle schools
highlights.detail: Discovery, East, Liberty, Pioneer, and West serve the middle grades.

highlights.label: 3 P-CEP high schools
highlights.detail: Canton, Plymouth, and Salem share one campus, courses, and a common P-CEP calendar clock.

highlights.label: 1 alternative high school
highlights.detail: Starkweather Academy supports alternative high-school completion and adult learners on a separate quarterly calendar.

highlights.label: 305-acre P-CEP campus
highlights.detail: The district identifies it as Michigan's only educational park.

highlights.label: About 6,200 P-CEP students
highlights.detail: The Park's official profile reports roughly 6,200 students using the campus each school day.

districtFaqs.q: Do all P-CCS students have a half day on the first day?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. The first K-12 student day is a half day. Kindergarten then has two additional half days while grades 1-12 attend full days.

districtFaqs.q: What time does a P-CCS half day end?
districtFaqs.a: The family calendar lists 12:10 p.m. for elementary, 11:30 a.m. for middle school, 10:35 a.m. for a regular P-CEP half day, 10:40 a.m. for a P-CEP exam day, and 11:25 a.m. for Starkweather.

districtFaqs.q: Are Canton, Plymouth, and Salem separate high-school campuses?
districtFaqs.a: They are three comprehensive high schools sharing the 305-acre Plymouth-Canton Educational Park. Students have a home school but can take courses across the three buildings.

districtFaqs.q: Does a K-5 half day affect P-CEP students?
districtFaqs.a: No. A K-5-only half day changes the elementary schedule. Middle-school and P-CEP students follow their regular day unless the calendar names their grades too.

districtFaqs.q: Does Starkweather Academy follow every date on the P-CCS family calendar?
districtFaqs.a: No. The district family PDF lists Starkweather bell times, but the academy publishes a separate four-quarter calendar with its own registration, records, conference, incentive, and graduation dates.

districtFaqs.q: Why does P-CCS link a Wayne County common calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Wayne County's common calendar coordinates selected professional-development and break dates among 33 districts. P-CCS still publishes its own family calendar for local opening, half-day, conference, testing, and finals details.

districtFaqs.q: Can families subscribe to a live P-CCS calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. The official district calendar page links a Google Calendar subscription containing days off, half days, district events, and updates. Individual school calendars are still needed for building events.

customSections.label: The Five P-CCS Half-Day Clocks
customSections.content: Both reviewed family calendars publish the same level-specific start and dismissal times. The P-CEP exam-day row matters because it differs from the regular P-CEP half day.

table.footnote: Check the live district and school calendars in case P-CCS changes bell times after publication.

customSections.label: District Calendar, P-CEP, and Starkweather Are Different Layers
customSections.content: The one-page family calendar is the districtwide K-12 baseline. P-CEP adds campus schedules, activities, and course details across three high schools, while Starkweather's separate calendar controls its quarter-specific attendance dates.
